Definition: from G1722 and G4043; to perambulate on a place, i.e. (figuratively) to be occupied among persons:--walk in.
BiblicalUsage: A single, beautiful use: in 2 Corinthians 6:16 God says, I will dwell in them, and walk in them — the God who lives among His people also moves among them, as He walked in the garden of old.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God does not visit His people from a distance — He dwells in them and walks in them, and that nearness is what makes us His people.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
